From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Stone <matthew.stone@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 May 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan — performance checkpoint and tuning next steps

Matt — thanks for the dump. I reviewed the CSV and pulled an initial summary below. We should discuss on Friday's checkpoint, but wanted to capture quick findings and owners so we can act before the close window.

Quick findings (from acme_latency_summary_q2.csv, profiling window: 90s steady-state):
- Median token latency: 22ms (good)
- 95th percentile token latency: 125ms when sequence length <= 512
- 99th percentile spikes to ~520ms during bursts at 8 concurrent streams (observed during KV cache misses)
- Aggregate throughput: 1,800 tokens/s on the current node type (A100s w/ q4f16 profile)

Risks / observations:
- Tail spikes correlate with concurrent cache loads and token-generation bursts (likely KV cache eviction/rehits)
- Batching windows currently at 12ms; increasing helps throughput but adds ~10–25ms median latency for short requests
- Quantization to q5_0 reduces memory pressure but introduces slight quality regressions on long sequences (we have eval prompts showing 2–3% drop in rouge-like metric)

Proposed next steps (owners + ETA):
1) Priyom: run a short canary with KV prewarm enabled for 8-stream scenario and capture tail latencies; due Wed 2028-05-04 EOD. (attachment: acme_latency_summary_q2.csv referenced)
2) Marissa: produce prompt-set eval comparing q4f16 vs q5_0 on Acme's 12 canonical prompts; due Thu 2028-05-05 noon.
3) Aditya: test increasing batching window to 20ms on a staging pool and measure P50/P95/P99; collect perf traces by Thu 2028-05-05 EOD.
4) Kimberly: aggregate results and propose a tuned profile for production cutover by the next checkpoint (Fri 2028-05-09).

Meeting request: Friday 10:00am PT for a 30-minute MAP checkpoint (calendar invite to follow).

Attachments: acme_latency_summary_q2.csv (CSV, 120KB)

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
